# RG20 `missing-citation`: A cited contract or function is not in the pinned target

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** error (error; runs only when --target and --target-commit are set)

An import path, contract name or called function in the PoC is not present in the target tree at the pinned commit.

## Why it matters

The other rules read the test. They do not open the protocol. A PoC can import `src/Vault.sol` and call `inventedDrain` when neither exists at the commit the report cites. This rule reads that tree, at that commit, and checks the names the test uses. It does not run the test and it does not decide that the bug is real.

## How to fix it

Pass `--target` as the protocol checkout and `--target-commit` as the commit the report cites. Drop citations that are not in that tree, or fix the path so it matches a file at that commit.

## Fires on

```solidity
import {Vault} from "src/Vault.sol";
vault.inventedDrain();
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
import {Vault} from "src/Vault.sol"; // this file and withdraw() exist at the commit
vault.withdraw(1);
```

## How it can be wrong

- A helper the test defines itself, or a forge-std name (`Test`, `Vm`). Those are not looked up in the target.
- A function the test calls through an interface the tool could not tie to one contract. The name is then required to exist on some contract in the tree, so a shared name (`transfer`) passes and a name that exists nowhere fails.
- The commit is required. Without `--target` and `--target-commit` this rule does not run, and a clean result still does not mean the citations were checked.

## In Solana tests (Rust and Anchor TypeScript)

Not checked. Solana tests are not checked against a pinned program crate yet. The citation check reads Solidity.

## In Move tests (Sui and Aptos)

Not checked. Move tests are not checked against a pinned package. The citation check reads Solidity imports and calls.

## Silencing it

An `allow` comment in the repo under review does not silence this rule, and neither does a `realism.yaml` or `realism-gate.toml` inside that repo. Policy is an operator file outside the tree (`--declaration`, `--config`). `--trust-inline-allows` is the author switch, for a PoC you wrote and are not gating.

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG20) <why this is not a defect here>
```

The comment is the same in Rust, TypeScript and Move. A comment without a reason is ignored even with `--trust-inline-allows`, and the output says so.
